examples.scenario: Adversary performs a model poisoning attack by injecting maliciously crafted training samples into a public dataset repository used for training an image classification model. The injected samples contain subtle pixel perturbations and mislabeled data that cause the model to misclassify specific attacker-chosen images as a target class (backdoor).

indicators: Sudden abnormal increase in training samples for a specific class in dataset version control logs
Presence of samples with suspiciously high pixel noise or perturbation beyond expected augmentation levels
Label flipping detected (e.g., cat images labeled as dog) in training data
Unexpected drop in validation accuracy despite increased training data
Anomalous high-confidence misclassification of clean test samples consistent with backdoor trigger
examples.detection_method: Implement automated data pipeline monitoring that flags abnormal label distribution shifts and checks pixel-level noise statistics of new training data batches. Use embedding similarity analysis to detect outlier samples. Monitor model validation metrics for sudden drops. Employ adversarial training and data sanitization tools to detect poisoned data signatures.
